gloss: emphasis line drawn beside text; (in horizontal writing) underline

definitions.gloss: emphasis line drawn beside text; (in horizontal writing) underline
definitions.explanation: A line drawn next to a passage to mark it out. In vertical Japanese writing it runs down the right side of the characters; in horizontal writing it appears as an underline.

examples.japanese: {大事|だいじ}なところに{傍線|ぼうせん}を{引|ひ}いた。
{傍線|ぼうせん}の{部分|ぶぶん}を{現代語|げんだいご}に{訳|やく}しなさい。
examples.english: Translate the underlined portion into modern Japanese.

notes:
Composed of {傍|ぼう} (beside) + {線|せん} (line) — literally a line at the side, reflecting vertical writing, where emphasis marks go alongside the characters rather than underneath them.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {傍線|ぼうせん}を{引|ひ}く: to draw an emphasis line
- {傍線|ぼうせん}{部|ぶ}: the marked portion
- {傍線|ぼうせん}の{箇所|かしょ}: the passage with the line beside it
- {傍線|ぼうせん}は{筆者|ひっしゃ}による: emphasis added by the author

USAGE:
Most often met in exam questions and academic quotations, where {傍線|ぼうせん}{部|ぶ} ("the marked portion") identifies the passage a question is about. In everyday horizontal text, {下線|かせん} (underline) is the more usual word.
